title: Language Advantage Is a Function of the Executor: criteria self-audit and undecidability audit in cross-language code generation by LLM coders (timetable-ab)
description:
Original proposition. When the executor is an AI large language model, does Lisp have a measurable language advantage? Eleven candidate levers were pre-registered and tested with 7 languages, 81 runs and 36 invariants, each invariant first proven able to go red before it was allowed to say "pass".

This is a restructured version of v1.0. Conclusions are now reported with a three-way verdict — established / refuted / undecidable — and two files were added: CONDITIONS.md (the conditions required to decide the question, and which of them are missing) and experiments/timetable-ab/results.tsv (one machine-readable row per run; columns that need human judgement are left empty rather than guessed).

Three-way result. Established (3): expansion-time rejection (19/19 invariants green with validation off vs. load-time failure with it on); zero ceremony cost (all three arms, 0/0 manual edits); live-image REPL saves characters (9028 → 5957). Refuted (3): S-expressions are not the most compact (CL 7506 vs JS 5933 characters at 5 ops); skill-pack intervention showed no main effect (0/6); at 15 ops the Common Lisp implementation is 1.93× the JavaScript one. Undecidable (6): every remaining lever, for the reasons below.

Missing conditions, stated plainly. C1 no weak-executor channel — only a strong model was available; 1.5B–7B tiers do not run on the author's machine and no external quota was available, so the entire P>0 half of the question was never observed. C2 no exclusive machine or clock alignment — all timing data is void and the crossover point N* is undecidable. C3 a single model family — language effect cannot be separated from training-distribution effect. Two further items are incomplete rather than missing: C4 nine surviving mutants (coverage of silent-failure detection unknown) and C5 scale (≤30 ops, ≤1k lines; no extrapolation to larger projects).

Three things this dataset does not do. It does not read "not detected" as "not present"; it does not extrapolate beyond the measured scale; it does not delete data — the timing columns, the retired line-count metric and all nineteen recorded failures of the measurement apparatus remain in the chronicle, annotated with their scope.

Included: 81 run artefacts, 14 frozen specifications, the 36 invariants with their go-red proofs, mutation scores with sample-size bounds and the twelve mutation floors, CONDITIONS.md, results.tsv with RESULTS-SCHEMA.md, a 2318-line append-only chronicle, and CLAIMS.md — one row per claim, with the command that checks it, the file it writes and the boundary it holds under. Excluded: compiled binaries, build caches, machine-local temporary files, personal data.

Intended use: replication of the measurement protocol; reuse of the mutation-testing gate as a way to audit one's own criteria; and an empirical basis for benchmark-validity work in LLM code generation.
notes: v1.1.0 published 2026-10-30. v1.1.1 (same day) erratum: an earlier note claimed a 2-character discrepancy between the chronicle (11460) and results.tsv (11458) for run "audit-lisp". False alarm: 11460 belongs to "scale-lisp", 11458 to "audit-lisp"; chronicle and table agree. The retraction is recorded rather than silently corrected. v1.1.1 also adds CLAIMS.md (a 29-row verification table with per-claim command, output file, status and boundary) and records an unresolved item: re-running gate.cjs reports scale-lisp as 0% with a red baseline, so claim-21 is downgraded to undecidable pending investigation. v1.1.2 erratum E-03: the claim that hand-written JSON in Common Lisp was the most compact across languages is RETRACTED (holds under line count only). The headline 1.93x is downgraded to a three-factor composite (ecosystem share of I/O, task shape requiring JSON I/O, and a design confound: the CL arm is a macro DSL while the JS arm is table-driven). Core to core is 1.36x. See metric-split.cjs and claim-9b. v1.2.0 adds the v3 experiment (PROTOCOL-v3.md, check-v3.cjs with 36 invariants, two reference implementations, 12 independent generations, results-v3.tsv). Headline: with the same implementation style, JS/CL character ratio is 0.97x (inline) and 0.81x (abstract) -- the 1.93x was a composite of unequal styles plus JSON ecosystem. Abstraction saves 28-40% characters but concentrates failure: first-pass 6/6 inline vs 2/6 abstract. T1 corrected: the symbolic layer changes the correlation structure of errors, not the mean error rate. v1.3.0 adds the incremental and maintenance arms. Same 30 ops, three operations: build (macro/inline = 0.62 chars), append one op (0.56 chars/op), change one cross-cutting rule (--dry: 2 vs 30 edit sites, ratio 0.07). Eight data problems documented in the addendum. v1.3.1 reclassification fix: lever 8 (S-expressions are cheaper to READ) had been judged with a WRITE metric. That is a metric mismatch; lever 8 moves from "refuted" to "untested". Recorded as problem 9 of 9. v1.4.0 structural rewrite after a full audit. LAYER A (reproducible): 4 cells regenerated with per-cell prompt.txt, a frozen spec and checker (sha256 in FREEZE-reproducible-layer-v3.1.txt), plus one clean failure chain (macro 5/36 -> 33/36 -> 36/36). LAYER B (exploratory): the previous 101 runs, of which only 1 had a prompt.txt, retained as observations only. Twenty-one problems enumerated in six classes. claim-32 (first-pass determined by scheme) RETRACTED: its failures landed on two checks (#32, #36) the frozen spec did not state. T1 kept, risk side rests on a single clean sample. v1.5.0 (2026-10-31) adds RESULTS-AUDIT-v3.3.md and a 20-case sharp checker (check-v4.cjs, 76 cases total) plus two new experiments. (a) MAINTENANCE RADIUS, now reproducible: starting from two 30-op implementations that pass all 51 non-dry checks, one cross-cutting rule (--dry) was added with only the rule text given, never the location. macro arm: 0 of 30 op bodies touched, 2 structural sites in the driver layer, 3 rewritten existing lines, 4 diff hunks, +292 chars. inline arm: 28 op branches + 2 sites, 439 rewritten lines, 34 hunks, +514 chars. Ratio on op-layer edits: 0 to 28. Chain-of-2 prerequisites documented: the argv prefilter must recognise the prefix, and the state must be a single re-bindable root (otherwise an in-place setf defeats the binding swap). (b) SELF-CHECK VALUE (Appendix A), same spec / same 76 checks / same model family, only the checking protocol varying: no-self-check macro = 0/76 (compile-time collapse); self-check allowed = 76/76, 76/76, 70/76. The 70/76 case ran MORE self-checks than the 76/76 case (6 compiles, ~320 runs, 149 self-built cases, all green) and still failed 6 checks, all on one unstated ambiguity (camel-case verb spelling). Finding: self-check removes implementation errors, not interpretation errors; its ceiling is the quality of your own criteria, not the tooling. Five design biases are now enumerated (D1 no-self-check, D2 op names colliding with CL exports 5/30, D3 dry pre-included, D5 camel-case naming), all biased against the Lisp arm only. Theory updated: T1b becomes a SYMBOLISATION risk -- abstraction lifts names into symbols, symbol namespaces collide with the language's own, and the collision is invisible to reading but visible to find-symbol; the risk is a function of whether the executor checks symbols, not a fixed cost. v1.5.1 (2026-10-31) ERRATUM E-04 -- a checker error that could never fail. Checks #37-#51 encoded `ok swapTeacher 2` (camel case), while the frozen spec states at line 39 that `verb` is the LOWER-CASED command name. Most implementations copied the camel-case spelling straight from the op table as well. The checker and the implementations were therefore wrong in the same direction, so no amount of execution could surface it. After fixing the six expectations the numbers become: v3.2 four cells 56/56 -> 50/56 each (same six violations); C-group baselines 51/51 -> 45/51, post-rule 76/76 -> 70/76; D1 self-check cells 76/76, 76/76, 70/76, 70/76, 70/76, 70/76 (no-self-check cell unchanged at 0/76). NEW RESULT from the same fix: only 2 of 8 independent implementations honoured a rule the spec states explicitly (75% violation rate), and all six violators had run substantial self-checks (2-6 compiles, 90-320 executions, 26-149 self-built cases). Self-check did not even prompt reading that line: each implementation tested "does my code match my understanding", and the understanding came from the op table, not from the rule. UNCHANGED: character ratios (0.92 / 0.81 / 1.39 / 1.58) and the C-group maintenance radius (0 op bodies : 28, 3 : 439 rewritten lines, 4 : 34 hunks), because character counts and edit sites do not depend on output casing. This is the sixth checker error in the series and the first whose class is different: errors 1-5 were wrong expected values, exposed by running an existing implementation; error 6 was a missed line of spec, missed by the checker and by the implementations alike. The lesson recorded is that the last line of defence for criteria is a line-by-line reading of the spec, not self-testing. v1.5.2 (2026-10-31) documentation-only release; no data or criteria changed. Adds SPEC-AUDIT.md: a 16-row table that walks every hard requirement in the frozen spec and names the check that covers it. Any row without a check number must either gain a check or be registered as a known gap before a spec freeze is allowed. Writing that table immediately surfaced two more gaps: spec L61 ("no trailing spaces, end with LF") and spec L124 ("must not depend on the current working directory") have NO covering check at all. Both are registered. Also carries: the retraction banner on RESULTS-AUDIT-v3.3 (all pass rates there are superseded by v3.4), three new CLAIMS rows (claim-37 spec-compliance 2/8, claim-38 checker-and-implementation can miss the same line, claim-39 "four cells all green" no longer holds), and the two-layer report now opens with an erratum E-04 section. Reason for publishing separately from v1.5.1: the correction letter to a prospective host states that this manual step now exists, so the artifact must be retrievable at the concept DOI rather than promised in prose. v1.5.3 (2026-10-31) criteria extended from 76 to 80 cases and one v3.1 observation retracted. SPEC-AUDIT immediately paid off a second time: three more explicit spec rules had no covering check at all -- teacher/loc may be "-" (spec L24), name/teacher/loc are 1-12 characters (only the 13-character rejection was tested, never the 12-character acceptance), and "-" must be overwritable by edit. Checks #77-#80 added. Re-run with 80 cases: two cells reach 80/80, ten cells 74/80 with the same six camel-case failures, one cell 0/80 (compile-time collapse). Specification compliance is 2 of 13 implementations. RETRACTED: the v3.1 observation that "self-check intensity and outcome are not monotonically related". It rested on the E-04 faulty checks. Under corrected criteria the most heavily self-checked cell (6 compiles, ~320 executions, 149 self-built cases) is one of the two 80/80 cells. The correct statement is: self-check intensity does correlate with outcome, and the six remaining failures have nothing to do with self-check intensity -- they track only whether the implementer read spec line 39.
